definition_zh: 假装；装作；声称；自称拥有；（游戏中）扮演；假装的
definition_en: to act as if something is true or real when it is not, or to claim a right or title for yourself
core_image: 一个人抬手在脸前撑起一块看不见的布，把表情挡在后面
scene: 午后的客厅里，孩子把几个靠垫围成一圈，说那是自己的城堡，母亲站在门边没有拆穿。The boy liked to pretend that the cushions were the walls of a castle.
sceneCN: 这里 pretend 是「假装、装作」（第 1 个义项：明知不真，却演得像真的一样）；句意为男孩喜欢假装靠垫就是城堡的墙。图中可辨识物件：围成一圈的靠垫、客厅地毯、站在门边的母亲。

collocations.zh: 假装游戏（儿童想象性游戏）
想象中的朋友（儿童虚构的同伴）

derivatives.zh: 由 pretend 的同族名词形构成，义为「假装；借口」，英式英语常写作 pretence
由 pretend 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「觊觎王位者；冒充者」
由 pretend 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「假装的；虚假的」

senses.title: To act as if something is true when it is not
senses.definition: to behave as if something is true or real while knowing that it is not
senses.definitionCN: 明知某事不真，却表现得像真的一样
senses.example: He pretended to be asleep when his mother opened the door.
senses.exampleCN: 母亲开门时，他假装睡着了。
senses.why: Latin praetendere meant to stretch something out in front of the body, and a made-up manner works exactly like that screen: it stands between you and the people looking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praetendere 本义是「把东西伸到身前」，而装出来的样子正像这样一块挡在身前的帘子，隔开自己和看过来的人，所以「假装」是这个动作最直接的用法。

senses.title: To claim a right or title for oneself
senses.definition: to put forward a claim to a right, title, or quality, often with little support
senses.definitionCN: 对某项权利、头衔或品质提出主张，常缺乏充分依据
senses.example: The young duke pretended to the throne after his uncle died.
senses.exampleCN: 叔父去世后，那位年轻的公爵声称王位应归自己。
senses.why: The oldest sense is holding something out in public and saying it is yours; a claim is that gesture performed with words instead of hands.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是把东西当众举起来、说它属于自己；所谓「声称拥有」，就是把这一动作改用言语来完成，手不必真的伸出去。

senses.title: To act out an imagined situation in play
senses.definition: to imagine that a scene is real and act it out, as children do in play
senses.definitionCN: 想象某个情境是真的并把它演出来，如儿童游戏中所为
senses.example: The children pretended that the sofa was a boat on the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把沙发当成一条船，假装在海上航行。
senses.why: Once the word means putting on a show, children's play becomes its natural home, because nothing in the scene has to be true for the scene to work.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词等于「演一场戏」，儿童游戏就成了它最自然的场所：布景不必为真，戏照样能演下去，所以「扮演」这一支从「假装」里长出来。

senses.title: Imaginary, used before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for something that exists only in play or in the imagination
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，形容只存在于游戏或想象中的事物
senses.example: Her daughter invented a pretend friend who lives under the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她女儿虚构了一个住在楼梯下的假想朋友。
senses.why: English often presses a verb into service as a modifier; a scene that is only performed needs a word to mark it as not real, and the bare verb does that job.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动词直接拿来当修饰语；一段只在戏里存在的情境，需要一个词标明它并非真实，而光秃秃的动词正好担起这个差事，于是有了形容词用法。

intro.en: Pretend goes back to a Latin verb for stretching something out in front of you; the modern sense of a false show grew out of that gesture of holding a screen before the body.
intro.cn: pretend 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「把东西伸到身前」的动词；现代「假装」的义项，正是从「在身前撑起遮挡」这个动作长出来的。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front of, and it marks whatever is placed ahead of the body.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，标示被放到身体之前的东西。

items.en: The verb tendere meant to stretch or hold out, and it is the source of a large English family about stretching toward something.
items.cn: 动词 tendere 意为「伸展、伸出」，英语中一大族表示「朝某处伸展」的词都出自它。

items.en: Praetendere joined the two: to stretch something out in front, whether a cloak, an excuse, or a claim.
items.cn: praetendere 把两者合起来：把某物伸到前面，那可以是斗篷，也可以是借口或主张。

items.en: Old French pretendre meant to claim or assert, and English took that meaning over in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 pretendre 意为「声称、主张」，英语在十四世纪接受了这个意思。

items.en: From claiming something openly, the word slid toward claiming what is false, and later to children acting out a scene that never happened.
items.cn: 从公开声称某事，词义滑向声称不实之事，后来再指孩子在游戏里演出一段并未发生的情境。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for stretching; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for putting on a false appearance.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「伸展」的动词展开；近义组收其他表示「装出假相」的动词。

entries.definition: A false claim or excuse, or the act of pretending.
entries.definitionCN: 虚假的声称或借口，也指假装这一行为。

entries.definition: A person who claims a title or position that is not theirs.
entries.definitionCN: 声称拥有不属于自己的头衔或地位的人；觊觎者。

entries.definition: A claim to importance or merit that is usually not deserved.
entries.definitionCN: 对重要性或优点的声称，通常并无资格。

entries.definition: A false reason given to hide the real one; it comes from a Latin verb meaning to weave, so it is only close in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 为掩盖真实原因而给出的假理由；它来自表示「编织」的拉丁动词，与本词只是拼写、读音接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To make something false look real, or such a thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 让假的东西看起来像真的，也指这样的假货。

entries.definition: To pretend to have a feeling or an illness.
entries.definitionCN: 假装有某种感受或疾病；佯称。

entries.definition: To imitate the appearance or conditions of something.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿某物的外观或状况。

entries.definition: To pretend to be someone else, usually in order to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 假扮成别人，通常为了欺骗。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix of place and a verb of stretching, and its family keeps returning to what is held out in front of a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀和表示「伸展」的动词构成，同族词都围绕「伸到人前的东西」展开。

normal.en: Praetendere literally means to stretch something out in front, so the oldest picture is a screen held before the body.
normal.cn: praetendere 字面就是「把东西伸到前面」，最古老的画面是一块挡在身前的帘子。

normal.en: Tendere, the stretching verb, also gives extend, intend and tension, all of them about pulling or holding out.
normal.cn: 表示伸展的 tendere 还给出 extend、intend、tension，都跟拉长、伸出有关。

normal.en: Pretense is the noun of the same family: the false front itself rather than the act of putting it up.
normal.cn: pretense 是同一词族的名词，指那层假门面本身，而不是撑起门面的动作。

normal.en: Pretender keeps the older sense of claiming: a person who says a title belongs to them.
normal.cn: pretender 保留了「声称」的旧义：一个说某个头衔属于自己的人。

normal.en: The adjective pretend sits before a noun, as in pretend play, because it labels a whole scene rather than describing an action.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 pretend 站在名词前，如 pretend play，因为它标注的是一整段情境，而不是描述动作。

abstract.en: A screen in front of the body explains both branches: you hide behind it, and you also point to it as proof.
abstract.cn: 身前的帘子能解释两条分支：你躲在它后面，也指着它当凭证。

abstract.en: Pretending is not quite lying, because both sides may know the scene is invented.
abstract.cn: 假装不完全是说谎，因为双方可能都知道这场情境是编出来的。

abstract.en: Children do openly what adults do carefully: build a world, then live in it for an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 孩子把大人小心做的事公开做出来：搭起一个世界，然后整个下午住在里面。

examples.en: He pretended to be asleep when his mother opened the door.
examples.cn: 母亲开门时，他假装睡着了。

examples.en: The young duke pretended to the throne after his uncle died.
examples.cn: 叔父去世后，那位年轻的公爵声称王位应归自己。

examples.en: Her daughter invented a pretend friend who lives under the stairs.
examples.cn: 她女儿虚构了一个住在楼梯下的假想朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「扑来疼」——先扑到地上，再喊一声疼，整套动作都是装出来的。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ tendere（伸展）构成 praetendere，本义「伸到前面、举起示人」，经古法语 pretendre 进入英语；「举出主张」引申为「声称」，再引申为「假装」。注意 tendere 是「伸展」，与 prevent 所用的 venire（来）不同源，两词只共享前缀 prae-。

sensesIntro.en: The core gesture is holding something out in front of the body; the senses move from a public claim to a false show, then to play, then to the adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是把东西举到身前；义项从公开的主张，走向虚假的展示，再走向游戏，最后是形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raising a screen between the face and the people watching.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在脸和旁观者之间举起一块遮挡物。

branches.en: a child closing his eyes and calling it sleep
branches.cn: 孩子闭上眼，说自己在睡觉

branches.en: cushions turned into castle walls
branches.cn: 靠垫被当成城堡的墙

branches.en: a nobleman pointing at a throne and naming it his
branches.cn: 贵族指着王座说那是自己的

branches.en: a sofa sailing across an imagined sea
branches.cn: 沙发在一片想象的海上航行

branches.en: a friend who lives under the stairs
branches.cn: 一个住在楼梯下的朋友

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place, a Latin verb of stretching, and the English endings that name the false front and the person who claims.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示「伸展」的拉丁动词，以及命名假门面与声称者的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to stretch out in front, to put forward

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch out in front, to allege

definition_zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服
definition_en: to be widespread or dominant, to win out over opposition, or to persuade someone to act
core_image: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下
scene: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下。Westerly winds prevail over the pass for most of the year.
sceneCN: 这里指风与天气长期占主导（第 1 个义项：风与天气盛行）；句意为西风一年中大部分时间控制着这个山口。图中可辨识物件：山口、旧旗、旗杆、被风压弯的草；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「盛行的；普遍的」
由「盛行」的形容词加名词尾构成，义为「盛行；普遍程度」
由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「占优势的；盛行的」
由「占优势的」形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「占优势地」
与拉丁语「valere」同族，经法语进入英语，义为「有用；有帮助」

senses.title: Of wind and weather
senses.definition: to blow steadily or to be the usual weather of a place and season
senses.definitionCN: 指风持续地吹，或成为某地某季的常况
senses.example: Dry winds prevail across the plateau in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季高原上盛行干燥的风。
senses.why: The earliest English uses describe forces that hold the air, because prevailing is first about what dominates a place.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的用法描述控制空气的力量，因为「盛行」首先指在某地占主导。

senses.title: Of customs and ideas
senses.definition: to be widely found or generally accepted among a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中广泛存在或被普遍接受
senses.example: The custom still prevails in the mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在山村里仍然盛行。
senses.why: Once a usage holds a region the way weather does, the verb extends from air to habit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一种做法像天气那样占住一个地区，这个动词就从空气扩展到习惯。

senses.title: To win an argument
senses.definition: to prove stronger than the opposing case in a debate or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论或争执中证明比对方的主张更强
senses.example: Common sense prevailed after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间辩论，常理占了上风。
senses.why: Being stronger is the core of the Latin verb, and an argument is a contest of strength between claims.
senses.whyCN: 「更强」是拉丁动词的核心，而争论正是各种主张之间的力量较量。

senses.title: To win a contest
senses.definition: to defeat opponents in a match, a race or a struggle
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、竞速或斗争中击败对手
senses.example: The home side prevailed in the final minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在最后几分钟取胜。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal and military verb for the side that turns out stronger.
senses.whyCN: 体育界借用了这个法律与军事动词，指最终更强的一方。

senses.title: To persuade someone
senses.definition: to bring someone round to a course of action by argument or appeal
senses.definitionCN: 通过论证或请求使某人接受某种做法
senses.example: She prevailed on the committee to reopen the case.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服委员会重新审理此案。
senses.why: Persuasion is winning a person over, so the preposition on marks the one who is overcome.
senses.whyCN: 说服就是把一个人争取过来，因此搭配的介词标出被说服的那一方。

senses.title: Of effort that succeeds at last
senses.definition: to succeed after sustained pressure, patience or repeated attempts
senses.definitionCN: 在持续施压、耐心等待或反复尝试之后取得成功
senses.example: Patience and evidence finally prevailed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心与证据最终奏效。
senses.why: The verb can name an impersonal force that wins, even when no person is doing the winning.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以指一种非人的力量取胜，即使并没有人在取胜。

senses.title: Of an old rule that outlives its reason
senses.titleCN: 旧制度延续而缘由已失
senses.definition: to remain in force long after the purpose it once served has disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 在当初的用途消失很久之后仍然有效
senses.example: The old rule still prevails long after its purpose vanished.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧规定在用途消失很久后仍然有效。
senses.why: What prevails simply holds its ground, whether or not anyone can still explain why.
senses.whyCN: 「盛行」的东西只是守住自己的位置，不管还有没有人能解释缘由。

senses.title: To win in a court of law
senses.definition: to succeed in a legal action or to establish a right against the other party
senses.definitionCN: 在法律诉讼中成功，或对另一方确立一项权利
senses.example: The tenant prevailed in the housing dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 租户在住房纠纷中胜诉。
senses.why: Legal language keeps the old sense of a stronger claim carrying the day.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言保留了旧义，即更强的主张最终获胜。

intro.en: Prevail comes from Latin prae-, before or beyond, and valere, to be strong or to be worth, forming praevalere, to be stronger. English took it through French in the fourteenth century; the family of valere also includes valid, value and avail.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语前缀「prae-」「在前、超出」与「valere」「强、有价值」，合成「praevalere」「更强」。英语于十四世纪经法语引入；「valere」的同族词还包括「valid」「value」「avail」。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or to be worth, and it described health, power and value alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为强壮或有价值，同时描述健康、力量与价值。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or beyond, marking a position ahead of others.
items.cn: 前缀意为「在前」或「超出」，标出比别人更靠前的位置。

items.en: Prae plus valere gave praevalere, to be stronger, whose past stem is praevaluī.
items.cn: 前缀加动词得到「praevalere」「更强」，其过去词干为「praevaluī」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English, where it was spelled and pronounced in several ways before settling.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带到英语，其拼写与读音经过几种形式才固定下来。

items.en: English used prevail first for holding power or influence, and soon for winning a contest.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词表示掌握权力或影响力，很快也用于表示在较量中获胜。

items.en: Courts fixed the sense of winning a case, while ordinary speech kept the weather, custom and persuasion senses.
items.cn: 法庭固定了「胜诉」义，而日常口语保留了天气、习俗与说服诸义。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like prevail; the second group names neighbouring ideas of dominance, victory and persuasion.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「prevail」相近；第二组是与「支配、取胜、说服」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for what is dominant or most common, as in the prevailing wind.
entries.definitionCN: 指占主导或最常见的形容词，如盛行风。

entries.definition: Widespread in a place or at a time, often used of diseases or beliefs.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地某时广泛存在的，常用于疾病或观念。

entries.definition: The fact or degree of being widespread.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛存在的事实或程度。

entries.definition: To be useful or helpful; it shares the Latin strength word.
entries.definitionCN: 指有用、有帮助；共用同一个拉丁「强」词。

entries.definition: Bravery in battle, from the same Latin word for strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指战斗中的勇猛，出自同一个表示力量的拉丁词。

entries.definition: To hold the most power or influence in a place or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地或某种情境中掌握最大的权力或影响。

entries.definition: To be the largest or most noticeable element among others.
entries.definitionCN: 指在其他要素中数量最多或最显著。

entries.definition: To win a decisive victory, often with a sense of celebration.
entries.definitionCN: 指取得决定性胜利，常带庆祝意味。

entries.definition: To convince someone to believe or do something.
entries.definitionCN: 指说服某人相信或去做某事。

entries.definition: To continue in existence or action, close to the sense of an old rule still holding.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续存在或继续行动，接近旧规定仍然有效那一义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin strength word behind prevail, its real family and its fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后表示「强」的拉丁词、真实同族词与固定搭配。

normal.en: Praemia and prevail share a Latin idea: the stronger thing stands, and the stronger claim wins.
normal.cn: 奖品与盛行共享一个拉丁观念：更强的东西站住，更强的主张获胜。

normal.en: The prefix means before or beyond, and the stem means strong, so prevail is to be stronger than what stands in front.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在前、超出」，词干意为「强」，所以这个词指比挡在前面的东西更强。

normal.en: Prevail on someone is the fixed pattern for persuasion, with the preposition on before the person.
normal.cn: 劝说某人用的是固定模式，介词放在人前面。

normal.en: The prevailing wind is the weather phrase, and it is the oldest kind of use.
normal.cn: 盛行风是天气方面的说法，也是最古老的一类用法。

normal.en: Valid, value and avail all descend from the same Latin word for being strong or worth something.
normal.cn: 有效的、价值与有用都出自同一个表示「强或有价值」的拉丁词。

abstract.en: Prevailing is not shouting loudest; it is being the thing that is still standing when the wind drops.
abstract.cn: 盛行不是喊得最响，而是风停之后仍然立着的那一个。

abstract.en: An old rule prevails because nobody remembers how to remove it, not because it is right.
abstract.cn: 旧规定之所以延续，是因为没人记得怎样废除它，而不是因为它正确。

abstract.en: To prevail is to make the world agree with you without having to raise your voice.
abstract.cn: 占上风是让世界同意你，而不必提高嗓门。

examples.en: Cooler air will prevail over the region by the weekend.
examples.cn: 到周末，较凉的空气将控制这一地区。

examples.en: The older interpretation prevailed among historians for a century.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag that bends in a steady gale but never falls, because the stronger force holds its ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面旗在稳定的大风里被压弯却从不倒下，因为更强的力量守住了位置。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: one wind or one kind of weather holds a place for most of the year.
branches.cn: 天气：一种风或一类天气在一年的大部分时间里占住一个地方。

branches.en: THE LONG HABIT: a custom spreads widely, and an old rule stays after its reason is gone.
branches.cn: 长久的习惯：习俗广泛流传，旧规定在缘由消失后仍留下。

branches.en: THE STRONGER CLAIM: an argument wins out, and a side wins the match.
branches.cn: 更强的主张：一种论点占上风，一方赢下比赛。

branches.en: THE OVERCOMING: a person is persuaded, and patient effort succeeds at last.
branches.cn: 争取与奏效：一个人被说服，耐心的努力最终成功。

branches.en: THE COURT: the stronger legal right carries the case.
branches.cn: 法庭：更强的法律权利赢得案件。

intro.en: Prevail is a Latin verb built from a prefix of position and a stem of strength, and English keeps both pieces in a whole family.
intro.cn: 这是一个由位置前缀与力量词干构成的拉丁动词，英语在两个成分上都保留了一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere supplies the strength, prae- supplies the advantage, and praevalere joins them into one verb.

senses.title: Being widespread
senses.definition: the quality of existing widely in a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 在某地或某群体中广泛存在的性质
senses.example: The prevalence of mobile phones changed how people queue.
senses.exampleCN: 手机的普及改变了人们排队的方式。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus valere 'be strong' gives praevalere, 'to be stronger, prevail'. What prevails is everywhere, so prevalence names wide existence.
senses.whyCN: prae-“在前”加 valere“强壮”构成 praevalere“更强、占优势”。占优势者处处都在，因此 prevalence 命名“广泛存在”。

senses.title: Epidemiological prevalence
senses.definition: the proportion of a population that has a disease or condition at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻人群中患某病或具备某状况的比例
senses.example: The prevalence of diabetes in the region is eleven percent.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区糖尿病的患病率是百分之十一。
senses.why: Epidemiology needed a word for how much disease is present now, as distinct from how fast new cases appear.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学需要一个词指“现在有多少病”，以区别于“新病例出现得多快”。

senses.title: Prevalence versus incidence
senses.definition: the stock of existing cases, contrasted with incidence, the flow of new cases
senses.definitionCN: 现有病例的存量，与发病率所指的新增病例流量相对
senses.example: Prevalence stays high even when incidence falls, because patients live longer.
senses.exampleCN: 即使发病率下降，患病率仍可能很高，因为病人活得更久。
senses.why: The stock-and-flow distinction is the core of epidemiology. Prevalence counts all who have it; incidence counts all who get it.
senses.whyCN: 存量与流量之分是流行病学的核心。患病率统计所有正患病者，发病率统计所有新患病者。

senses.title: Prevalence rate
senses.definition: the numerical ratio of cases to the whole population, often expressed per hundred thousand
senses.definitionCN: 病例与总人口之比，常以每十万人计
senses.example: Prevalence rates are hard to compare across countries with different testing.
senses.exampleCN: 检测水平不同的国家之间，患病率很难比较。
senses.why: A rate needs a denominator. The word supplies the idea of proportion, and the phrase supplies the arithmetic.
senses.whyCN: 比率需要分母。这个词提供比例的概念，短语提供算术。

senses.title: Prevalence of an idea
senses.definition: the extent to which a belief, custom or practice is found among people
senses.definitionCN: 某种观念、习俗或做法在人群中被发现的程度
senses.example: The prevalence of the custom surprised the visiting researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗的普遍程度让来访研究者感到意外。
senses.why: Social science borrows the medical word: beliefs spread and persist like infections, so the same measure applies.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学借用医学词：观念像感染一样传播与留存，因此可用同一度量。

senses.title: Point versus period
senses.definition: in epidemiology, the contrast between prevalence measured at one moment and over a stated period
senses.definitionCN: 流行病学中在某一瞬间测量与在某一时期内测量的对照
senses.example: Point prevalence counts cases on the day of the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 时点患病率统计调查当天的病例。
senses.why: The window defines the count. A snapshot and a season give different numbers from the same population.
senses.whyCN: 窗口定义计数。快照与一整季，从同一人群得到不同数字。

senses.title: Statistical proportion
senses.titleCN: 统计比例：总体中的占比
senses.definition: the fraction of a defined population showing a characteristic at a stated time
senses.definitionCN: 在指定时间，某一界定人群中具备某特征的比例
senses.example: Prevalence is a proportion, so it always lies between zero and one.
senses.exampleCN: 患病率是比例，所以总在零与一之间。
senses.why: Statistics reduces the word to a proportion with a clear numerator and denominator, which is why it can be plotted and compared.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把词化简为有明确分子分母的比例，因此它能被画图与比较。

senses.title: Prevalence in public debate
senses.titleCN: 公共讨论中的“有多普遍”
senses.definition: used in policy argument to claim that a problem is common and therefore demands action
senses.definitionCN: 在政策论证中用来声称某问题很普遍，因而需要行动
senses.example: The prevalence of food insecurity was used to justify the new programme.
senses.exampleCN: 粮食不安全问题的普遍性被用来为新计划辩护。
senses.why: Numbers persuade. Calling a problem prevalent does rhetorical work beyond describing frequency.
senses.whyCN: 数字有说服力。把问题称为“普遍”，除了描述频率，还有修辞作用。

intro.en: Prevalence comes from Latin praevalere 'to be stronger, prevail', from prae- 'before, beyond' plus valere 'to be strong'. The noun is praevalentia.
intro.cn: prevalence 来自拉丁 praevalere“更强、占优势”，由 prae-“在前、超过”加 valere“强壮”构成，名词为 praevalentia。

items.en: valere meant 'to be strong, be well, be worth'. It gives value, valid and valour, all built on strength or worth.
items.cn: valere 意为“强壮、健康、有价值”。它产出 value、valid、valour，都建立在“力量”或“价值”上。

items.en: prae- 'before, beyond' plus valere produced praevalere, 'to be stronger than, prevail'. The prefix marks superiority, not time alone.
items.cn: prae-“在前、超过”加 valere 构成 praevalere“强过、占优势”。前缀标记优势，不只是时间。

items.en: The abstract noun praevalentia named superior force or wide influence. Late Latin used it for what holds sway.
items.cn: 抽象名词 praevalentia 指优势力量或广泛影响。晚期拉丁语用它指“占主导地位者”。

items.en: English borrows prevalence in the 1600s for the quality of being widespread or dominant.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 prevalence，指“普遍存在或占优势”的性质。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries public health fixes the technical sense: the proportion of a population with a condition.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，公共卫生固定了技术义：人群中患某状况的比例。

items.en: Sociology and economics extend it to beliefs and behaviours, where spread can be measured the same way.
items.cn: 社会学与经济学把它扩展到观念与行为，其扩散可用同样方式测量。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the val- stem or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group all concern how common something is, differing in measurement.
note.cn: 形近组共享 val- 词干或 pre- 前缀；近义组都关心“有多常见”，差别在度量方式。

entries.definition: widespread or dominant. The adjective describes the thing; prevalence names the fact or the rate.
entries.definitionCN: 普遍的；流行的。形容词描述事物，prevalence 命名事实或比率。

entries.definition: to be widespread, or to win out. It names the holding of ground that prevalence then measures.
entries.definitionCN: 盛行；占优势。它命名占据优势的过程，prevalence 则度量它。

entries.definition: sound or legally effective. It comes from valere 'be strong' but means 'having force', not 'being common'.
entries.definitionCN: 有效的；正当的。同出 valere“强壮”，但意为“有力量”，不是“普遍”。

entries.definition: the rate at which new cases appear in a period. It measures flow, while prevalence measures stock.
entries.definitionCN: 发病率。它度量新病例的流量，而 prevalence 度量存量。

entries.definition: the rate of occurrence of events. It counts repetitions, while prevalence counts how many are affected.
entries.definitionCN: 频率。它统计事件重复次数，而 prevalence 统计受影响的人数比例。

entries.definition: the quality of occurring often. It is the everyday equivalent, without the technical denominator.
entries.definitionCN: 常见性。它是日常说法，没有技术上的分母。

entries.definition: the state of being most powerful or influential. It stresses control, where prevalence stresses spread.
entries.definitionCN: 支配地位。它强调控制力，而 prevalence 强调扩散范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: valere 'be strong' plus pre- 'beyond' gives 'strong enough to hold everywhere', hence 'widespread'.
normal.cn: valere“强壮”加 pre-“超过”，得“强到处处站得住”，即“普遍”。

normal.en: Prevalence is a stock; incidence is a flow. The bathtub picture makes the difference concrete.
normal.cn: 患病率是存量，发病率是流量。浴缸的比喻让差别变得具体。

normal.en: The adjective prevalent is the everyday form: a prevalent belief is one that prevails.
normal.cn: 形容词 prevalent 是日常形式：“流行的看法”就是占上风的观念。

normal.en: Prevalence rate always has a denominator, which is why the phrase appears in every epidemiology paper.
normal.cn: 患病率总有分母，所以这个短语出现在每篇流行病学论文里。

normal.en: Point prevalence and period prevalence differ only in the time window used for counting.
normal.cn: 时点患病率与时期患病率只差在计数所用的时间窗口。

abstract.en: Picture a stain spreading across paper until most of the sheet is coloured.
abstract.cn: 想象一片污渍在纸上扩散，直到大部分纸面都被染上颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a bathtub: the water level is prevalence, the tap is incidence, the drain is recovery.
abstract.cn: 想象一个浴缸：水位是患病率，水龙头是发病率，排水口是康复。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd where every tenth person wears the same hat.
abstract.cn: 想象人群里每十个人就有一个人戴同样的帽子。

examples.en: The prevalence of smoking has fallen among teenagers.
examples.cn: 青少年吸烟的普遍程度已经下降。

examples.en: Prevalence counts everyone who has the condition, not only new cases.
examples.cn: 患病率统计所有正患该病的人，而不只是新病例。

examples.en: Researchers compared the prevalence of the habit across four regions.
examples.cn: 研究者比较了这一习惯在四个地区的流行程度。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞沃伦斯”音近 prevalence：普普通通的东西“沃”得到处都是、连成一片——遍地都有 → prevalence 普遍存在

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all ask how much of something is present in a frame, and the differences come from the frame and the arithmetic.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在问“某个框里有多少这种东西”，差别在框与算法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one colour spreading until it covers the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种颜色扩散到几乎盖满地图。

branches.en: SPREAD: phones and customs are both measured by how widely they are found.
branches.cn: 扩散：手机与习俗都按“分布多广”来衡量。

branches.en: STOCK AND FLOW: prevalence counts existing cases, incidence counts new ones, and the two answer different questions.
branches.cn: 存量与流量：患病率数现有病例，发病率数新病例，回答不同问题。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: a rate and a proportion are the same fraction seen as a number or as a share.
branches.cn: 算术：比率与比例是同一个分数，一个看成数值，一个看成占比。

branches.en: WINDOWS: point and period prevalence differ only in when the counting happens.
branches.cn: 窗口：时点与时期患病率只差在计数的时间。

branches.en: PERSUASION: calling a problem prevalent turns a frequency into an argument for action.
branches.cn: 说服：把问题称为普遍，就把频率变成了行动理由。

intro.en: Prevalence is prae- plus valere plus -entia. The prefix marks superiority, the verb marks strength, and the suffix makes an abstract noun.
intro.cn: prevalence 由 prae- 加 valere 加 -entia 构成。前缀标记优势，动词标记力量，后缀构成抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere 'be strong' yields praevalere 'prevail' and praevalentia 'prevalence'. The same valere gives value, valid and valour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 valere“强壮”产出 praevalere“占优势”与 praevalentia“普遍”。同一 valere 还产出 value、valid、valour。

items.meaningCN: 普遍；流行程度（-ence 抽象名词）

senses.title: Common in a group
senses.titleCN: 普遍的：在这群人中到处都有
senses.definition: found widely among the members of a particular group
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定群体的成员中广泛存在
senses.example: The fear of public speaking is prevalent among new teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 害怕当众讲话在新教师中很普遍。
senses.why: prevalere means 'to be stronger, prevail'. What prevails over a group is found throughout it, so the adjective describes wide presence.
senses.whyCN: prevalere 意为“更强、占优势”。在一群人中占优势的东西遍布其中，因此形容词描述“广泛存在”。

senses.title: Dominant opinion
senses.definition: currently accepted or believed by most people, whether or not it is correct
senses.definitionCN: 当前被多数人接受或相信的，无论是否正确
senses.example: The prevalent view was that the climate would not change.
senses.exampleCN: 当时占上风的看法是气候不会改变。
senses.why: The word reports strength of acceptance, not truth. A prevalent error is still prevalent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词报告的是被接受的程度，不是真伪。普遍的错误依然“普遍”。

senses.title: Medical frequency
senses.titleCN: 医学上的常见：病例很多
senses.definition: describing a disease or condition that affects a large share of a population
senses.definitionCN: 描述影响大量人口的疾病或状况
senses.example: The disease is prevalent in areas without clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病在没有清洁水源的地区很常见。
senses.why: Public health uses the adjective where prevalence is high: the condition is not rare, so it changes policy.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生在患病率高时用这个形容词：该状况不罕见，因此会影响政策。

senses.title: Dominant wind or weather
senses.titleCN: 主导风向：常刮的那一股
senses.definition: in meteorology, describing the wind direction most often recorded in an area
senses.definitionCN: 气象学上描述某地出现最多的风向
senses.example: The prevalent wind in July comes from the southwest.
senses.exampleCN: 七月的主导风来自西南。
senses.why: Weather statistics use prevalence as frequency dominance: the direction that prevails is the one that comes most often.
senses.whyCN: 气象统计把“普遍”当作“频率占优”：占上风的风向就是出现最多的那个。

senses.title: Prevailing custom
senses.titleCN: 盛行的习俗：多数人这么做
senses.definition: describing a practice or custom that most people in a society follow
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个社会中多数人遵循的做法或习俗
senses.example: Early marriage was prevalent in the village a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 一个世纪前，早婚在这个村子里很盛行。
senses.why: Customs spread by imitation, so the social version of the word measures how many people copy a behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠模仿传播，所以这个词的社会版本度量“有多少人照着做”。

senses.title: Commonest form
senses.titleCN: 最常见的形态：多数属于这一类
senses.definition: describing the most frequent type or variant within a category
senses.definitionCN: 描述某一类别中最常见的类型或变体
senses.example: The prevalent form of the gene differs by region.
senses.exampleCN: 该基因的常见形态随地区而异。
senses.why: Biology counts variants, so prevalent marks the variant with the largest share rather than with the greatest power.
senses.whyCN: 生物学统计变体，所以 prevalent 标记占比最大的那一种，而非最强的那一种。

senses.title: Legal 'prevailing' party
senses.titleCN: 法律上的胜诉方（相关用法）
senses.definition: in legal usage, the related participle prevailing describes the side that wins; prevalent itself means common
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语中相关分词 prevailing 指胜诉一方，而 prevalent 本身意为“普遍”
senses.example: The prevailing party may recover costs.
senses.exampleCN: 胜诉方可以收回诉讼费用。
senses.why: The two forms split: prevailing keeps the courtroom sense of winning, while prevalent keeps the statistical sense of being common.
senses.whyCN: 两个形式分工：prevailing 保留法庭上“胜出”的义，prevalent 保留统计上“常见”的义。

senses.title: Contrast with rare
senses.definition: occupying the high end of a frequency scale, opposed to rare or uncommon
senses.definitionCN: 处在频率刻度的高端，与罕见、少见相对
senses.example: Such storms are prevalent in autumn but rare in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的风暴在秋季常见，在春季罕见。
senses.why: A scale needs both ends. Prevalent is only meaningful against rare, which is why the two words so often appear together.
senses.whyCN: 刻度需要两端。prevalent 只有与“罕见”对照才有意义，所以两词常一起出现。

intro.en: Prevalent is the adjective from Latin praevalere 'to be stronger, prevail' (prae- 'before, beyond' + valere 'be strong'), with the ending -ent from Latin -ent-.
intro.cn: prevalent 是拉丁 praevalere“更强、占优势”（prae-“在前、超过”+ valere“强壮”）的形容词形式，词尾 -ent 来自拉丁 -ent-。

items.en: valere meant 'to be strong, be well, be worth'. It also gives value and valid, so the family is about strength and worth, not about quantity.
items.cn: valere 意为“强壮、健康、有价值”。它还产出 value 与 valid，因此这个词族关乎力量与价值，不关乎数量。

items.en: prae- 'beyond' plus valere gives 'to be stronger than'. The verb first meant winning, then holding sway generally.
items.cn: prae-“超过”加 valere 得“强过”。动词先指取胜，后泛指占据优势。

items.en: the present participle praevalens 'prevailing' became the adjective source for English prevalent.
items.cn: 现在分词 praevalens“占优势的”成为英语 prevalent 的形容词来源。

items.en: English adopts prevalent in the 1500s, first for something having great force or influence, then for something widespread.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪采用 prevalent，先指“有强大力量或影响”，后指“广泛存在”。

items.en: Modern usage fixes the quantitative sense: a prevalent disease is one with many existing cases.
items.cn: 现代用法固定了数量义：“常见病”就是现有病例很多。

items.en: In ordinary speech prevalent now simply means common, and its natural partner is rare.
items.cn: 在日常口语中，prevalent 现在就是“常见”，它的天然搭档是“罕见”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares val- or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group all say 'common', differing in tone and scale.
note.cn: 形近组共享 val- 或 pre- 前缀；近义组都表“常见”，差别在语气与尺度。

entries.definition: the fact of being widespread or the measured rate. The noun names the state; the adjective describes the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 普遍存在或测得的比率。名词命名状态，形容词描述事物。

entries.definition: current, dominant, or winning. It often modifies wind, opinion or a legal party, and stresses current dominance.
entries.definitionCN: 当前的；主导的；胜诉的。常修饰风、意见或法律当事方，强调当下占优。

entries.definition: intended to stop something from happening. It shares pre- but comes from venire 'to come', not valere.
entries.definitionCN: 预防性的。它共享 pre- 前缀，但来自 venire“来”，并非 valere。

entries.definition: occurring often or shared by many. It is the everyday word, with no trace of 'prevailing force'.
entries.definitionCN: 常见的；共同的。它是日常词，不带“占优势力量”的痕迹。

entries.definition: found over a large area. It stresses geography, while prevalent can stress a group or a period.
entries.definitionCN: 分布广泛的。它强调地理范围，而 prevalent 可强调群体或时期。

entries.definition: most powerful or noticeable. It stresses control, while prevalent stresses how many share something.
entries.definitionCN: 占支配地位的。它强调控制，而 prevalent 强调有多少人共有。

entries.definition: widespread, usually of something bad. It adds a negative judgment that prevalent does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 猖獗的；充斥的。通常指坏事，带有 prevalent 所没有的负面判断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: The verb prevail means 'to hold sway', so prevalent describes what holds sway across a group.
normal.cn: 动词 prevail 意为“占上风”，所以 prevalent 描述“在一群人中占上风”的东西。

normal.en: prevalent among and prevalent in are the two frames: one for people, one for places.
normal.cn: 与人群连用、与地点连用是两个框架：一个接人群，一个接地点。

normal.en: The noun prevalence supplies the rate; the adjective supplies the description.
normal.cn: 名词 prevalence 提供比率，形容词提供描述。

normal.en: A prevalent wind is simply the wind that blows most often, which shows the scale meaning clearly.
normal.cn: 主导风就是刮得最多的风，清楚显示了“频率占优”的含义。

normal.en: Its natural opposite is rare, and the pair often appears in the same sentence.
normal.cn: 它的天然反义是“罕见”，两者常出现在同一句里。

abstract.en: Picture one style of doorbell on every house along a street.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上每家每户都装同款门铃。

abstract.en: Picture a weather vane that points the same way on most days of the year.
abstract.cn: 想象风向标在一年大多数日子指向同一方向。

abstract.en: Picture a colour that fills most of a mosaic, leaving a few tiles of another shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一种颜色占满马赛克的大部分，只留下几块别的颜色。

examples.en: The practice is prevalent in coastal villages.
examples.cn: 这一做法在沿海村庄很普遍。

examples.en: Malnutrition remains prevalent in the drought zone.
examples.cn: 营养不良在旱区依然普遍。

examples.en: The prevalent assumption turned out to be false.
examples.cn: 那个普遍接受的假设最终被证明是错的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞沃伦特”音近 prevalent：普普通通“沃”得到处都是、连成一“特”——到处都有 → prevalent 普遍的

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前、超过”+ valere“强壮”→ praevalere“占优势”；praevalent- 词干 + -ent 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all say that something is found in many places or many people, and the differences come from what is being counted.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都说“某物在许多地方或许多人身上出现”，差别在被计数的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one style repeated on every street corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个街角都重复着同一种样式。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CUSTOM: a fear among teachers and an early-marriage custom are both widely copied behaviours.
branches.cn: 人群与习俗：教师的恐惧与早婚习俗都是被广泛模仿的行为。

branches.en: DOMINANCE: a prevailing view and a prevailing wind both hold sway by being the most frequent.
branches.cn: 占优：主导看法与主导风都因最常见而占上风。

branches.en: COUNTED POPULATIONS: disease cases and gene variants are measured by share.
branches.cn: 被计数的人群：病例与基因变体都按占比衡量。

branches.en: LEGAL SPLIT: prevailing keeps the courtroom sense of winning, while prevalent keeps the statistical sense.
branches.cn: 法律分工：prevailing 保留法庭“胜诉”义，prevalent 保留统计义。

branches.en: SCALE: common only means something against rare.
branches.cn: 刻度：常见只有对照罕见才有意义。

intro.en: Prevalent is prae- plus valere plus -ent. The prefix marks superiority, the verb marks strength, and the suffix makes the adjective of a participle.
intro.cn: prevalent 由 prae- 加 valere 加 -ent 构成。前缀标记优势，动词标记力量，后缀把分词构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere 'be strong' → praevalere 'prevail' → praevalens 'prevailing'. English keeps the stem prevalent- and adds no new prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 valere“强壮”→ praevalere“占优势”→ praevalens“占优势的”。英语保留 prevalent- 词干，未加新前缀。

items.example: The custom is prevalent in the south.
items.exampleCN: 这一习俗在南方很盛行。

items.example: The value of the house rose.

definition_zh: 阻止；防止；使无法；妨碍；预防
definition_en: to stop something from happening, or to make it impossible for someone to do something
core_image: 有人还没走到门口，一条手臂已经横在门框上把路挡住
scene: 雨天路滑，小区门口新铺了一道减速带，旁边立着一块提示牌。The speed bump was installed to prevent accidents at the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 prevent 是「预防、防止发生」（第 3 个义项：采取措施，使事故一类的事不发生）；句意为这道减速带是为了防止门口发生事故而设。图中可辨识景物：减速带、雨后的路面、提示牌。

pos.zh: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍

derivatives.zh: 由 prevent 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「阻止；预防」
由 prevent 加 -ive 构成，义为「预防的；防护的」
由 prevent 加 -able 构成，义为「可预防的；可以避免的」

senses.title: To stop an event from taking place
senses.definition: to stop an event or action before it can happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事件或行动来不及发生
senses.example: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
senses.exampleCN: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。
senses.why: Latin praevenire meant to come before someone; arriving at a place first is what lets you stand in the way of what follows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevenire 意为「先于某人到来」，先一步赶到某处，才有机会挡在后头那件事的前面，所以「阻止」是「先来」的直接结果。

senses.title: To make it impossible for someone to act
senses.titleCN: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍
senses.definition: to make it impossible for someone to do what they intended
senses.definitionCN: 使某人无法做成原本打算做的事
senses.example: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。
senses.why: Here no force is aimed at the person; the word only reports that an obstacle got there first and the action never began.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不对某人施加力量，只是说明障碍先到了，那个动作始终没能开始，所以介词 from 后面接的是被挡住的行动。

senses.title: To reduce the risk of illness or damage
senses.definition: to take action so that illness, damage, or trouble does not develop
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施，使疾病、损害或麻烦不致发展起来
senses.example: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。
senses.why: Medicine widened the focus from one event to a whole class of risk: acting early becomes a habit rather than a single block in a doorway.
senses.whyCN: 医学把焦点从单一事件扩大成一整类风险：提前动手变成习惯，而不再是门口一次性的拦阻，于是「预防」从「阻止」里独立出来。

senses.title: To go before, in older religious language
senses.definition: to go before or act ahead of someone, a sense kept mainly in old prayers
senses.definitionCN: 走在某人之前或先行行动，这一义项主要保留在古老祷词中
senses.example: The old prayer asks God to prevent us in all our doings.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老祷词祈求上帝在我们一切所行的事上先行引导。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin meaning surviving in English; modern usage narrowed the word, but the prayer book never changed.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义在英语里的遗留：字面上就是「走在前面」。现代用法把词义收窄了，祷词却一直没改，所以这个古老义项仍能读到。

intro.en: Prevent is built from a Latin prefix meaning before and the verb to come: to prevent is, quite literally, to get there first, and hindering grew out of that head start.
intro.cn: prevent 由表示「在前」的拉丁前缀与动词「来」构成：字面上就是「先到一步」；阻挡的义项，正是从这个抢先到达的动作长出来的。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, the same prefix that appears in predict and prepare.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，predict 与 prepare 也用了这个前缀。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it supplies the ven- seen in intervene, convene and event.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，intervene、convene、event 里的 ven- 都来自它。

items.en: Praevenire meant to come before someone, to arrive ahead of them, and so to anticipate or forestall.
items.cn: praevenire 意为「先于某人来到」，即赶在对方前头到达，因此引申为预先、抢先拦下。

items.en: Old French prevenir kept both the sense of arriving first and the sense of hindering by getting there early.
items.cn: 古法语 prevenir 同时保留「先到」与「因先到而阻挡」两层意思。

items.en: Modern English dropped the literal meaning and kept the result: something is prevented when it never gets to happen.
items.cn: 现代英语丢掉了字面上的「先到」，只留下结果：一件事始终没能发生，就是被 prevent 了。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for coming; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for blocking, avoiding and putting off harm.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「来」的动词展开；近义组收阻挡、避开与消解祸患的动词。

entries.definition: The act of stopping something before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前将其阻止的行为；预防。

entries.definition: Intended to stop illness or trouble before it starts.
entries.definitionCN: 意在疾病或麻烦开始前就加以阻止的；预防性的。

entries.definition: Able to be stopped before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 可以在发生前被阻止的；可预防的。

entries.definition: Coming before or anticipating something; used mainly in theology.
entries.definitionCN: 先于某事先行而来的；主要用于神学语境。

entries.definition: To keep away from something so that it does not happen to you.
entries.definitionCN: 远远避开某物，使它不落到自己身上。

entries.definition: To make progress or action difficult.
entries.definitionCN: 使进展或行动变得困难。

entries.definition: To turn something bad away before it arrives.
entries.definitionCN: 在坏事到来之前把它挡开。

entries.definition: To make someone decide not to act, usually through fear of the consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 使人因后果的威慑而决定不做某事。

entries.definition: To end an action that has already started.
entries.definitionCN: 使已经开始的动作停止。

normalIntro.en: The word puts a Latin prefix meaning before onto the verb to come, and its family keeps the picture of arriving first.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在表示「来」的拉丁动词前加上「在前」的前缀，同族词都保留着「先一步到达」的画面。

normal.en: Prae- plus venire: prevent is to come before, and only later to block because you got there first.
normal.cn: prae- 加 venire：prevent 本是「先来」，后来才因先到而挡住。

normal.en: The ven- of prevent means come, as in invent and convene; pretend has a different verb, tendere, meaning stretch, so the two share only the prefix.
normal.cn: prevent 里的 ven- 意为「来」，invent、convene 同此；pretend 用的是另一个动词 tendere（伸展），两词只共享前缀，词源并不相同。

normal.en: Prevention is the noun and preventive the adjective; both name stopping something ahead of time.
normal.cn: prevention 是名词，preventive 是形容词，两者都指提前挡住。

normal.en: Preventable marks what can be stopped, with the same -able heard in avoidable and curable.
normal.cn: preventable 标注「拦得住的」，后缀 -able 与 avoidable、curable 里的相同。

normal.en: The pattern「prevent somebody from doing something」keeps the image of a body standing in another person's way.
normal.cn: 搭配「prevent somebody from doing something」保留了「一个人挡在另一个人路上」的画面。

abstract.en: To prevent is to win a race nobody watches: the best prevention leaves nothing to see afterwards.
abstract.cn: prevent 是赢下一场没人观看的比赛：最好的预防，事后什么也看不见。

abstract.en: The word once meant arrive first, and every act of prevention is still a small race against an event.
abstract.cn: 这个词原本只表示「先到」，而每一次预防，仍是在和某个事件抢时间。

abstract.en: Prevent and pretend share a prefix but not a road: one comes first, the other stretches a screen.
abstract.cn: prevent 与 pretend 共享前缀，却不同路：一个抢先赶到，一个撑起帘子。

examples.en: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
examples.cn: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。

examples.en: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
examples.cn: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。

examples.en: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
examples.cn: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「扑来问」——人还没进门就先扑上去问一句，顺势把人拦在门外。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ venire（来）构成 praevenire，本义「先来、抢先到达」，引申为「预先阻挡」，经古法语 prevenir 进入英语。ve-nire 是「来」，与 pretend 所用的 tendere（伸展）不同源，两词只共享前缀 prae-。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arriving before something else; the senses run from stopping an event, to blocking a person, to forestalling illness, and finally to the old literal sense of going before.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「赶在某事之前到达」；义项从阻止事件，到挡住某人，到防病于未然，最后回到古老的「先行」本义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm raised across a doorway a moment before someone reaches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人还没走到门口，一条手臂已经横在那里。

branches.en: a hand shutting the window before the rain starts
branches.cn: 雨还没下，一只手先把窗关上

branches.en: a guard standing in a doorway with arms spread
branches.cn: 守卫张开手臂站在门口

branches.en: a needle given before the season of flu
branches.cn: 流感季节来临前打的一针

branches.en: an old prayer asking to be led from the front
branches.cn: 古老祷词求人先行引领

branches.en: a speed bump slowing every car at the gate
branches.cn: 减速带让门口每辆车都慢下来

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix of place to a Latin verb of coming, then adds English endings that name the act, the quality and the possibility.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示位置的拉丁前缀与表示「来」的拉丁动词结合，再加上命名行为、性质与可能性的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
